dishes.name: Tripes à la mode de Caen
dishes.desc: Beef tripe and ox foot simmered for hours with onions, carrots, leeks, cider and calvados. Caen's best-known dish, defended by a local brotherhood that holds a yearly tripe contest.
kw: tripes à la mode de caen

dishes.name: Salt-marsh lamb
dishes.desc: Lamb raised on meadows in Mont-Saint-Michel bay that the tides flood with seawater, which gives the meat a distinctive flavour. Eaten around the bay in Manche; the lamb holds AOC status.

dishes.name: Mont-Saint-Michel omelette
dishes.desc: A soufflé-style omelette of fresh eggs and salted Normandy butter, beaten and cooked in a long-handled pan over a wood fire. A fast pilgrim meal from the Mont-Saint-Michel inns since 1888.

dishes.name: Pont-l'Évêque
dishes.desc: Soft washed-rind cow's-milk cheese with a square shape and orange rind, from the Calvados department. One of Normandy's four AOP cheeses.

dishes.name: Teurgoule
dishes.desc: Rice pudding baked slowly for about five hours with milk, sugar and cinnamon until a dark crust forms. A traditional Lower Normandy dessert linked to the Granville area.
